title: Integrated 1M/2M Slumbot loss attribution with held-out solver proxy
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: A small set of general hand/state classes explains a replicated share of the 1M and 2M external losses across independent sessions, and at least one such class also has elevated disagreement from high-confidence Standard10+CFR4 consensus on held-out matched final states.
material_change: Zero-new-Slumbot hand-level discovery/confirmation attribution over the two audited 20k cohorts, followed by a label-free Standard10+CFR4 matched-state proxy gate; no learned weights or benchmark-specific rules are changed.
baseline: Seed1 1M scored -21.7592 bb/100 CI95 [-44.2479,0.7295]; Seed1 2M scored -38.02 CI95 [-59.4244,-16.6156]. Prior outcome-blind replay rejected simple Standard10-distance attribution, and bounded public-objective MGDA failed untouched breadth translation.
source: Audited raw hands from v6-integrated-seed1-1m-greedy-fresh20k-slumbot-20260903 and v6-integrated-seed1-2m-greedy-fresh20k-slumbot-20260903 plus CPU-exact state replay from v6-integrated-1m-2m-slumbot-state-drift-20260903.
notes: Sessions1-4 are discovery and sessions5-8 untouched confirmation in each corpus. Candidate classes are fixed in preregistration. Outcome tails are descriptive only; no Slumbot action or reward becomes a training target. Proxy support additionally requires elevated disagreement from high-confidence Standard10+CFR4 consensus in both confirmation corpora.

Post-hoc robustness, not used to change the preregistered decision: every leave-one-confirmation-session-out high-pot effect remained negative in both corpora. Approximate independent-binomial disagreement-uplift CIs were [+0.0267,+0.0624] at 1M and [+0.0151,+0.0475] at 2M.

The 39 high-confidence teacher-consensus disagreements in confirmed high-pot states were almost entirely on-policy all-in versus teacher check/call. Their observed outcome direction did not replicate: 1M had 24 hands net -70 bb, while 2M had 15 hands net +570 bb. This forbids interpreting the teacher action as a causal correction or using it as an action label.

result.summary: Across two independent 20k external cohorts, final-decision pots at least 30bb concentrated replicated losses and elevated high-confidence Standard10+CFR4 consensus disagreement. The preregistered class gate passed for this one class; all fold-related correlations failed the solver proxy.
result.conclusion: Large-pot states are a credible general coverage/value-calibration risk class: their negative excess survives every leave-one-session-out check and the policy differs from two general teachers more often there. However the specific all-in-versus-check/call discrepancy has opposite observed outcomes across 1M and 2M, so no action reversal, Slumbot label imitation, or direct solver-teacher patch is justified. The result localizes where to test internal critic calibration, not what action to take.
result.next_step: On fresh internal matched deals across multiple general opponents and both seats, measure terminal-return critic calibration and policy regret proxies stratified by pot/exposure, with special emphasis on final pots at least30bb. Compare the retained static-current-KL 1M endpoints with their parents and Standard10; only train a general high-pot resampling or value-calibration intervention if the internal defect replicates independently of Slumbot outcomes.
